ns2:section.sectionText: Multiculturalism in Clinical-Community Research and Practice- Multiculturalism is a popular topic and as aspiring psychologists it is important to stay up to date with its meaning and implications: personally, as a helping professional, in your research, and in your practice. In this course, we will discuss and define multiculturalism, understand individuals and your own reactions to multiculturalism, and discuss foundational frameworks that guide diverse approaches to integrating multiculturalism in clinical and community research and practice. This course involves reading required assignments, active class participation, and consistent completion of writing activities. Final grading for this course will be based on points earned for active class participation, completing assigned readings, writing assignments, literature reviews, topic development proposals, a final paper proposal, and a final individual poster presentation. RESTRICTED CLASS - Senior PSYC/BCOG (90 hrs earned) priority begins Nov. 2; Junior PSYC/BCOG (60 hrs earned) begins Nov. 9. All restrictions removed at 9:00 am on Nov. 11. **Elective course in Clinical/Community and Intradisciplinary Concentration**
